items.text: Bialgebra: $A$ with an algebra structure and a coalgebra structure $\pi$, $\pi$ and $\varepsilon$ being algebra homomorphisms.
Operation of a monoid on an affine space
$G\leftrightarrow A$ a monoid object, $X\leftrightarrow B$; an operation $G\times X\to X$ is a $k$-algebra homomorphism
\omega\colon B\to A\otimes B
Axiom $g(g'x)=(gg')x$: the two maps $G\times G\times X\to G\times X$, $(g,g',x)\mapsto(gg',x)$ and $(g,g',x)\mapsto(g,g'x)$, followed by $\omega$, agree. Dually:
\begin{CD} B @>{\omega}>> A\otimes B\\ @V{\omega}VV @VV{\pi\otimes 1}V\\ A\otimes B @>{1\otimes\omega}>> A\otimes A\otimes B \end{CD}
Axiom $1\cdot x=x$:
B\xrightarrow{\ \omega\ }A\otimes B\xrightarrow{\ \varepsilon\otimes 1\ }k\otimes B=B\ =\ \mathrm{id}_B
Neither axiom uses the multiplication of $A$ or $B$, only the $k$-module structures and $\pi,\varepsilon$.
$B$ is a comodule over the coalgebra $A$; here moreover $B$ is an algebra and all arrows are algebra homomorphisms.

Equivalent to a homomorphism $G\to\underline{\operatorname{Aut}}(X)$ ($\underline{\operatorname{Aut}}(X)$ for a group, $\underline{\operatorname{End}}(X)$ for a monoid) (general nonsense, any category); the diagrams are used for computations with rings.
Coalgebra of $\mathbb G_a$ and $\mathbb G_m$
k[t]\xrightarrow{\ \pi\ }k[t]\otimes k[t]=k[t',t''],\quad t'=t\otimes1,\ t''=1\otimes t
\mathbb G_a:\quad \pi(t)=t'+t''
Check: $\lambda',\lambda''\colon k[t]\to k'$ (i.e. $t'\mapsto\lambda'$, $t''\mapsto\lambda''$) composed with $\pi$ give $t\mapsto\lambda'+\lambda''$.
\mathbb G_m:\quad k[t,t^{-1}]\xrightarrow{\ \pi\ }k[t',t'',t'^{-1},t''^{-1}],\qquad \pi(t)=t't''
Linear operation of a group on a module
W(M)\colon k'\mapsto M\otimes_k k',\qquad G\to\underline{\operatorname{Aut}}_{\mathcal O}\bigl(W(M)\bigr)
$G(k')$ acts on the $k'$-module $M_{k'}$, functorially in $k'$, associatively, the unit acting as the unit.
Universal point $g\in G(A)$ ($=\mathrm{id}_A$) defines an $A$-linear automorphism $u$ of $M\otimes A$, i.e. a $k$-linear map
u_0\colon M\to A\otimes M
A point $g'\in G(k')$ is the image of $g$ by $A\to k'$; $u_{g'}$ is $u$ after base change $A\to k'$:
u_{g'}=(A\to k')_*\,u\colon M\otimes k'\to M\otimes k'
Unit axiom:
M\xrightarrow{\ u_0\ }A\otimes M\xrightarrow{\ \varepsilon\otimes 1\ }M\ =\ \mathrm{id}_M
Associativity (take $k'=A\otimes A$, the pair of points $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, $1\otimes x$); as written, the axiom for a right action (see 13 June, 5:13:35):
\begin{CD} M @>{u_0}>> A\otimes M\\ @V{u_0}VV @VV{\pi\otimes 1}V\\ A\otimes M @>{1\otimes u_0}>> A\otimes A\otimes M \end{CD}
Hence: a linear operation of $G$ on $M$ = a homomorphism $M\to A\otimes M$ satisfying these two diagrams; only the coalgebra structure of $A$ and $\varepsilon$ are used.
$M$ is a comodule over the coalgebra $A$; the category of $k$-modules on which $G$ operates = comodules over the coalgebra of $G$.
Same for a monoid $G$ (operation by endomorphisms; for automorphisms require $u$ invertible).
$G$ operating on an affine space $X\leftrightarrow B$: a comodule structure $B\to A\otimes B$ which is moreover a homomorphism of $k$-algebras.
Operation on the left of $X$ = operation on the right of $B$ (no distinction for a group, using inverses).
